meta.title: Adriana Mejía Cuartas — Board Chair, Global Coffee Platform
meta.description: Adriana Mejía Cuartas: Board Chair of the Global Coffee Platform and founder of Herencia VL. She designs and governs regenerative value chains in coffee, cocoa and palm.

sections.kick: Global Coffee Platform · Herencia VL · Haarlem, working worldwide
sections.name: Adriana Mejía Cuartas
sections.sub: Coffee doesn’t need another hero. <t>It needs better choreography.</t>
sections.note: Board Chair of the Global Coffee Platform. Founder and CEO of Herencia VL. Fourth generation of a coffee family from Manizales.

sections.label: The argument
sections.quote: Most projects here don’t fail for lack of money. <t>They fail because someone treated an adaptive problem as a technical one.</t>
body: A technical problem is solved with more resources. An adaptive problem is solved by changing the choreography between the people involved. Roughly eight in ten projects get that diagnosis wrong — and the cost of the error lands on the farm, not in the room where it was made.

Twelve and a half million coffee-growing families still live in poverty, after years of a growing conversation about sustainability. That distance between the conversation and the farm is the whole problem.

sections.label: Standing
sections.title: The rooms where <t>the decisions are made.</t>

items.d: Since 2024. More than 170 member organisations, across every major producing country. The platform turns ten in 2026.
Founded 2017 in the Netherlands. Impact investment, ESG and innovation in coffee, cocoa and palm value chains across Latin America and Africa.
Director for Europe. In 2015, the first woman in the Federation’s history nominated for its General Management, having travelled all fifteen coffee regions of Colombia.
First woman on its board. Fourth generation of a coffee family from Manizales; her mother was the first woman to represent her region at Colombia’s National Coffee Growers' Congress.

sections.label: Four structural barriers
sections.title: What stops good intentions <t>from reaching a farm.</t>
sections.intro: Not opinions about the sector. The four things that have to be answered before any programme can work.

rows.d: Nobody invests on a five- or ten-year view without a stable income. The horizon a regenerative transition requires is the one poverty makes impossible.
The producer does not know how the price of coffee is formed, or which climate risks are coming. Decisions are made where that information sits, and it does not sit on the farm.

rows.t: Institutions that fail, or fail to coordinate
rows.d: Several organisations arrive at the same farm with contradictory messages, and the producer is left to arbitrate between them.

rows.t: Women and young people left out of decisions
rows.d: Cultural exclusion from the rooms where things are decided — which removes from the table exactly the people who will still be farming in twenty years.

sections.label: How the work is done
sections.title: A sequence, <t>followed in order.</t>
sections.intro: Not a method with a name on it. The order that has produced programmes which outlast the person who designed them.

rows.d: Is this solved with more resources, or does it require changing the choreography between the actors? Everything downstream depends on getting this right.

rows.t: Map the stakeholders and the power
rows.d: Who decides. Who pays. Who implements. Who carries the risk. The asymmetries are identified before anything is designed.

rows.t: Design the what before the how
rows.d: Picture the programme finished, ten years out, before starting it — and define success in the producer’s terms rather than the donor’s.
Public capital, private capital, development cooperation and philanthropy, combined under a narrative umbrella wide enough to let the work scale.
Shared definitions, shared measurement, shared investment, shared accountability.
Programmes rarely fail at the start; they fail at the sustaining. The work is to build institutions that survive their leader.

sections.label: Trajectory
sections.title: Three layers, <t>built in sequence.</t>
sections.lede: The institution that formed her, the company she founded, and the global table she now chairs.

Maize programme with GIZ, German development cooperation — closed 2026

names: Board Chair. 170+ member organisations across Brazil, Colombia, Honduras, Indonesia, Kenya, Nicaragua, Peru, Tanzania, Uganda and Vietnam

The Coffee Sustainability Reference Code and its equivalence mechanism

sections.fn: Ten years in, there is more left to do than there is to celebrate.

sections.label: Where I serve
sections.title: Three ways of working, <t>three different rooms.</t>
sections.lede: Each with its own rhythm. All of them under her own name, and none of them a product.

cards.label: Boards
cards.title: Board and governance service
cards.desc: Global boards in agriculture, food and retail, and multi-commodity groups whose supply-chain resilience has become a governance question rather than a communications one.
items: Someone who has sat on both sides of the value chain

cards.label: Advisory
cards.title: Strategic advisory and executive accompaniment
cards.desc: For organisations investing in sustainability without seeing it arrive at the farm, and for the executives leading them.
items: By programme, or as a standing quarterly engagement

cards.label: Speaking
cards.title: Keynotes and moderation
cards.desc: Regeneration beyond the soil. Technical against adaptive. How more than a hundred and seventy stakeholders are moved as one.

sections.fn: I serve on few boards at a time, and I am fully present on the ones I take.
